articleMarkdown:
# Studying Héng (Duration): making worthwhile commitments sustainable

First check that the direction remains worthwhile, then continue at an appropriate pace; lasting does not mean never adjusting.

A forceful beginning does not necessarily lead to lasting effort. Héng discusses continuity, but also seeking too much depth too soon, persisting without results, and agitated exertion. It helps distinguish a steady commitment from rigid repetition: what you maintain, how you do it, and under what conditions all deserve examination.

## Identity and line order

Héng is hexagram 32 in the traditional King Wen sequence, with symbol ䷟. The lower trigram is Xùn ☴ and the upper trigram is Zhèn ☳; their traditional images are wind and thunder, respectively. Count the lines from the bottom: 初六、九二、九三、九四、六五、上六. A solid line is yang and a broken line is yin. Nine and six in the line labels designate yang and yin; they are not additional line numbers.

```text
━━━━ ━━━━  上六
━━━━ ━━━━  六五
━━━━━━━━━  九四
━━━━━━━━━  九三
━━━━━━━━━  九二
━━━━ ━━━━  初六
```

## Hexagram statement

恆：亨，无咎。利貞，利有攸往。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Duration: favorable progress, without blame. Steadfastness is beneficial; it is beneficial to have somewhere to go.

Legge understands Héng as continuing along an appropriate course. The benefit of having somewhere to go shows that continuity need not mean staying in place. Lasting requires a sound direction and action.

For a modern reflection, ask what you really want to preserve: a value, a commitment within a relationship, or a method that has long ceased to fit? Changing the method need not betray the original intention; sometimes it is what allows that intention to continue.

References: [zhouyi-32](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/恒&oldid=10646486), [legge1882-32](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## Interpretations in the Ten Wings

The Commentary on the Judgment and the Commentary on the Images belong to the commentarial collection known as the Yìzhuàn, usually called the Ten Wings. Below, these commentaries are kept separate from the hexagram and line statements, followed by modern learning applications.

The Commentary on the Judgment explains Héng through duration, discussing the changing seasons and beginnings that follow endings. The Commentary on the Images uses thunder and wind, then speaks of standing without changing direction. In the traditional account, direction and change are not simply opposites.

Today, write the aim clearly and allow arrangements to change with reality. Stability does not mean doing the same amount every day; it means honestly maintaining the necessary action after examining the conditions.

References: [zhouyi-32](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/恒&oldid=10646486), [hon-sep](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/chinese-change/)

## The six lines, from bottom to top

### 初六 · Demanding too much depth at the start may undermine continuity

浚恆，貞凶，无攸利。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Seeking depth in duration too soon: even firm correctness meets misfortune; nothing is beneficial.

Jùn suggests depth; Legge sees an excessive demand for permanence at the beginning. Turning intensity up to its maximum on the first day cannot guarantee continuity.

When rebuilding a writing habit, begin with a manageable scope. Requiring your best work every day too soon may prevent an actual practice from developing.

References: [zhouyi-32](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/恒&oldid=10646486), [legge1882-32](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九二 · A steady approach need not be dramatic

悔亡。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Regret disappears.

This line is exceptionally brief. The Commentary on the Images explains it through maintaining the center over time, and Legge also develops it through a central position and enduring appropriateness.

If an arrangement is working steadily, you need not keep changing methods just to appear to be progressing. Review actual results periodically and give effective elements time to work.

References: [zhouyi-32](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/恒&oldid=10646486), [legge1882-32](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九三 · Repeatedly abandoning principles affects trust

不恆其德，或承之羞，貞吝。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Not constant in one’s conduct, one may meet disgrace; even firm correctness brings regret.

Legge reads this as failure to sustain virtuous conduct, which may attract reproach. The emphasis is on consistency of behavior, not a demand never to acknowledge mistakes.

Alternately accepting and denying the same agreement makes cooperation difficult. If conditions really change, explain promptly and renegotiate instead of leaving others to guess.

References: [zhouyi-32](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/恒&oldid=10646486), [legge1882-32](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九四 · Persistence in the wrong place may bring no result

田无禽。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: No game in the hunting field.

A field with no quarry is a concise image of fruitless effort. Legge explains the lack of results through the line's position; he does not suggest that more time invested makes an approach more correct.

If a method has long failed to serve the aim, check whether it addresses the wrong object or lacks necessary conditions. Adjustment need not mean a lack of perseverance, and continuing should not be justified solely by past investment.

References: [zhouyi-32](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/恒&oldid=10646486), [legge1882-32](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 六五 · Recognize historical roles while preserving present-day autonomy

恆其德，貞，婦人吉，夫子凶。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Constancy in conduct, with steadfastness: good fortune for a woman, misfortune for a man.

This line gives different judgments according to ancient roles for women and men, and Legge also explains it within a marital hierarchy. We cannot erase the gender distinction and claim that the original expresses modern equality.

This article does not adopt a rule that women should obey and men should lead. Everyone in a lasting relationship can discuss what deserves continuity and when independent judgment and renegotiation are needed.

References: [zhouyi-32](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/恒&oldid=10646486), [legge1882-32](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 上六 · Constantly increasing effort is not necessarily stability

震恆，凶。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Agitated duration: misfortune.

The image of agitated duration carries movement and disturbance. Legge reads it as trying to force continuity through intense exertion.

If an arrangement can continue only through constant prompting and sacrificed rest, it deserves redesign. Genuine sustainability must fit people's capacities, rather than depend on pushing through time after time.

References: [zhouyi-32](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/恒&oldid=10646486), [legge1882-32](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## Helping a shared commitment last

Original modern scenario

Two friends agree to exchange reading reflections regularly. At first, they plan to discuss an entire book each week, but discover that they lack preparation time. They keep the aim of thoughtful reading and exchange, changing the arrangement to discussing a chapter at wider intervals.

When busy, they say so in advance and agree on another time. If several meetings cannot happen, they examine whether the format still fits, rather than simply blaming someone's lack of perseverance.

The modern value of Héng is giving commitments a clear, sustainable form. Revising an arrangement does not necessarily weaken a relationship; it may make it more genuine.

## Misreadings to avoid

- Héng does not require maintaining harmful, unfair, or unsuitable relationships, nor does it guarantee that persistence will succeed.

- The fifth line's historical gender rules need explanation and must not restrict anyone's choices today. The hexagram does not predict the length of a marriage or a career.

## Three practices

1. Write down the aim you truly want to preserve over time and the specific method you currently use to pursue it.

2. Check whether that method fits the available time, capacities, and wishes of those involved.

3. Set a reasonable point for review and decide what to maintain and what can change.

## Related hexagram

### Xián — Influence (hexagram-31)

Xián discusses being moved and responding to one another; Héng discusses continuing. A powerful beginning can be appreciated, while the conditions for continuity still need to be established separately.

## A closing question

While reading Héng, ask: am I continuing something valuable, or simply repeating a method that no longer fits?

## Textual note

The page path uses “恒”, while the classical text retains “恆”. The top line follows “震” in the base edition's main text; the page also lists the variant “振”.
